mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate at or below 3.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS <= 3.0% (over 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in unemployment rate above 5.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises above 5.5% (over 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous 3-month increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages signals robust consumer demand and labor market strength, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both > 12-month MA (3-month change)
evidence_refs: fact:Current PAYEMS at 133293.0 (t-1mo) and HOUST at 1837.0 (t-2mo)
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed 12-month MA (over 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (INDPRO > 120 and UNRATE < 5.0%), a 3-month rise in industrial production above 125 signals economic overheating and potential monetary tightening, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Current INDPRO at 118.527 (t-2mo) and UNRATE at 5.2% (t-1mo)
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where the late-cycle regime is active and INDPRO rises above 125 (over 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level above 1800 (thousands of units) indicates robust consumer demand for new homes, supporting household spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where HOUST > 1800 (over 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A 12-month CPIAUCSL annual change above 2.5% signals accelerating inflation, triggering monetary policy tightening and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Current CPIAUCSL at 193.2 (t-2mo) implies annual change near 2.5%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL annual change > 2.5% (over 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous 3-month increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages indicates strong consumer demand, supporting corporate revenue growth and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both > 12-month MA (3-month change)
evidence_refs: fact:Current RSAFS at 344895.0 (t-1mo) and HOUST at 1837.0 (t-2mo)
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where both RSAFS and HOUST exceed 12-month MA (over 5-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL annual change > 3.0%), a 3-month rise in federal funds rate above 3.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, reducing equity valuations and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Current CPIAUCSL at 193.2 (t-2mo) and FEDFUNDS at 2.79% (t-1mo)
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL annual change > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS rises above 3.5% (over 5-year rolling window).
